scope: Lung carcinoma, WHO Classification of Thoracic Tumours 5th ed. (2021). Histology gates which molecular tests are run, so the A<->B linkage is especially tight. Internal substrate only.

classification_records.morphology: Glandular/lepidic/acinar/papillary/micropapillary/solid patterns; graded by predominant + high-grade pattern (IASLC grading).
molecular_signature: the targetable-driver landscape lives here (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, etc.)
classification_records.grading_system: IASLC architectural grading (well/moderate/poor by predominant and high-grade patterns)
classification_records.clinical_note: The histology that carries nearly all actionable drivers; comprehensive molecular profiling is standard in advanced non-squamous NSCLC.

classification_records.morphology: Keratinization, intercellular bridges, or basaloid pattern.
molecular_signature: fewer targetable drivers; PD-L1 still relevant
classification_records.clinical_note: p40 is the key separator from adenocarcinoma. Targetable-driver yield is low, so PD-L1 and immunotherapy dominate biomarker workup.

classification_records.morphology: Small cells, scant cytoplasm, finely granular chromatin, nuclear molding, brisk mitoses and necrosis.
molecular_signature: emerging transcription-factor subtypes (ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, etc.)
classification_records.clinical_note: Distinct treatment paradigm; molecular subtyping is research/emerging. Distinguish from large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma.

classification_records.morphology: Large cells with neuroendocrine architecture (organoid, palisading, rosettes), high mitotic rate, necrosis.
molecular_signature: heterogeneous; SCLC-like and NSCLC-like molecular subsets
classification_records.clinical_note: Requires NE marker confirmation; biologically straddles SCLC and NSCLC.

classification_records.morphology: Organoid neuroendocrine architecture; typical vs atypical separated by mitotic count and necrosis.
classification_records.grading_system: Typical vs atypical carcinoid by mitoses + necrosis
classification_records.clinical_note: Well-differentiated NETs distinct from high-grade NEC; the mitosis/necrosis thresholds are the classification spine.

classification_records.entity: Adenocarcinoma in situ / minimally invasive adenocarcinoma (AIS/MIA)
classification_records.morphology: Pure lepidic growth (AIS) or lepidic with <=5 mm invasion (MIA).
defining_features: AIS: no invasion; MIA: <=5mm invasive focus
molecular_signature: EGFR mutations can be present early
classification_records.clinical_note: Excellent prognosis when fully resected; the lepidic-to-invasive spectrum is a common classification point.

notes: Histology determines molecular-test triage: actionable drivers concentrate in adenocarcinoma. p40 (squamous) vs TTF-1/napsin (adeno) is the foundational IHC split. Verify IASLC grading specifics at write time.
